correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the conditional split identities for Sackin \(S\), cherry count \(C\), and cherry-leaf depth sum \(Q\); the crucial mixed-term normalization has \((1-1/n)SC\) and \(-Q/n\). Exact marginal solutions for \(n\ge3\) give \(g_{n+1}=(1-1/n)g_n-2/9\) with \(g_3=0\), yielding the asserted rational formula. The initial \(n=2\) exception is explicit. An independent exact-rational enumeration of every unlabelled shape under the correct tip-splitting probability passed for sizes 2 through 10; enumeration alone was not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Sackin-index marginal moments, cherry marginal counts, and the cherry-pitchfork joint law are all prior work. Materially examined Cardona–Mir–Rosselló (arXiv:1202.6573, original results and 32-page PDF text), Dearlove–Frost (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004312, full HTML), Wu–Choi (arXiv:1508.03139, full HTML), and the 2020 depth-variance article. The closest same-pair paper explicitly says the Sackin and cherry statistics are weakly correlated but provides no exact \(\operatorname{Cov}(S_n,C_n)\) law. A rational all-size identity plus complete strict sign classification is not supplied by the inspected results nor implied by their separate marginals. General historical prior work could contain an equivalent implicit formula and independent priority verification remains open.
residual_risks: Older or unindexed formula for cherry–Sackin joint moments could already imply this exact identity without matching vocabulary.
No independent historical priority review is claimed.

The preceding literature contains same-pair qualitative observations; originality is specifically the explicit all-size rational law and its proof, not the observation that the pair is weakly correlated.

value.rationale: Sackin total tip depth and cherry count are established complementary phylogenetic shape statistics and are used jointly in asymmetry testing (Dearlove & Frost 2015). Prior work calls them weakly correlated but does not quantify their finite-sample mixed moment. The theorem gives a complete natural sign classification for every sample size and an exact linear covariance scale, permitting joint calibration, rather than a synthetic parameter slice or a re-expression of one marginal law.
